entries.title: Novel Resistance Training–Specific Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale Measuring Repetitions in Reserve
entries.claim: RPE scores tied to repetitions-in-reserve track intensity and support day-to-day load regulation.

entries.title: Application of the Repetitions in Reserve-Based Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale for Resistance Training
entries.claim: RIR-based RPE autoregulates load set-to-set to match daily readiness and proximity to failure.

entries.title: Accuracy in Estimating Repetitions to Failure During Resistance Exercise
entries.claim: Lifters estimate reps-to-failure within about one rep when sets are near failure (roughly 0–5 reps in reserve).

entries.title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass
entries.claim: Higher weekly set volume associates with greater hypertrophy; rep targets before load jumps align with volume-first progression.

entries.title: Warm-up revisited: the ramp method of optimizing performance preparation
entries.claim: Structured raise–activate–potentiate warm-ups prepare the athlete before working loads.
entries.note: Professional Strength and Conditioning 6:12–18; no DOI assigned.

entries.title: Temper warm-up percentage ladder
entries.claim: 40/60/80% of last working weight, snapped to available plates, is a practical barbell ramp.

entries.title: Temper plate increment table
entries.claim: Load jumps use equipment-aware minimum increments (barbell, pin stack, dumbbell step).

entries.title: Temper conservative opener
entries.claim: With no logged history, repeat the plan or last known numbers instead of inventing a heavier load.
